parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Hi Thomas, did you have a good time in Turkey?

Hi May, I had a great time, but I have to say, although I have always been being an archaeologist, before I went on an excavation, I used to find some of the things we did in class totally mystifying.

Me too. Before I did my trip to Egypt, I was often irritated at not being exactly what the lecturers meant. They were always so excited about everything.

Yeah, we did a lot of practical stuff on the excavation which I really needed. Was it harder than you expected?

Yes, mostly. I learned a lot more about the rules of archaeology. I was really taken aback by how precise you have to be with your data collection and recording. I took loads of photographs and they proved very useful, and the drawing went well too.

Yes, I think I’m quite good with the camera. I minded about the recording though. I had no idea it would take so much time.

Did you find anything particularly interesting when you were digging?

I did actually. I had to dig a trench in part of the site. Interestingly, there weren’t any bits of pottery there like you would expect to find, but I did get out some pieces of cloth and what looked like one or two silver beads. But our team leader said that they weren’t, they were probably lead weights for weaving. What about you?

I didn’t find anything myself, but quite a few of the other students did. What I enjoyed was trying to identify what crops the people who had once lived in the area had grown. They seemed to have had a much better diet than I expected — fish and wheat, as well as oats, honey and fruit, lots of different things.

Yes, it’s amazing, isn’t it? And from measuring the bones in one of the sites, that the people were actually taller and had better teeth than the people who live in the area today.

Probably due to less carbohydrates. How were the people you had to work with?

My team was great. They were made up of people my age from all over the world. It was good to work with them, lots of fun, and they taught me a lot. It was tough for us all though, getting up at dawn every day and being out until late afternoon.

Oh, that’s true enough. We were all exhausted, and I’d like to have an international team next time. Mine was mainly made up of English and Americans. I enjoyed the field school, but everyone was much more experienced and older than I was. It was a bit scary.

You know there’s going to be a question about the excavation projects in our test next week. Should we just run through it for practice?

Good idea. Our team leader was very strict about following the right procedure. He used to say, never excavate anything if you’re not sure it’s worth excavating. Now I think that when you’ve decided where to excavate, you go to the site hut and get whatever tools you need. Then clean the area, so you know exactly how big it’s going to be.

Right.

Okay. And you need to make sure you can remember what the site looks like before you begin digging.

I think photos are probably best for that rather than drawings at this stage.

I agree. You then attach them to a record sheet which you get from the team leader, remembering to put in the site code, unit number and time. So much red tape. You seem to spend half the time marking rather than digging.

That’s true. I think you then have to draw up a detailed plan of where you’re digging and then measure the limits.

And this is all before you actually start digging. Okay. So far, so good. Now you can start with the trowel. But first you have to get soil samples and you keep them for further analysis. Anything that you don’t think is useful, you leave in place on the site.

Yes. And if you make any finds, that is any object you retrieve, including animal bones, stone, as well as artefacts, they should all be registered and labelled.

And then you put them in a plastic bag and return them to the site hut.

That’s right. And remember to leave the tools and site hut as you would expect to find them.

Ha! Looks like we’ve learned something after all.

questions.question: How did Tomas and May both feel about parts of their studies before going on an excavation?

analyses.content: 男生提到去挖掘之前觉得课上的东西完全是“神秘的（mystifying）”，女生也表示她经常感到困惑，不知道讲师到底什么意思。

Hi May, I had a great time, but I have to say, although I have always been being an archaeologist, before I went on an excavation, I used to find some of the things we did in class totally mystifying. Me too. Before I did my trip to Egypt, I was often irritated at not being exactly what the lecturers meant.
你可能听到 excited（兴奋）想选 A，但录音里说的是“讲师们（lecturers）”很兴奋，而不是学生自己。

analyses.content: I was really taken aback by how precise you have to be with your data collection and recording. ... I minded about the recording though. I had no idea it would take so much time.
你可能听到 photographs（照片）想选 A，但男生只是说照片很有用，并没有说这让他感到“惊讶”或困难。
男生说被数据收集和记录必须非常“精确（precise）”吓了一跳，女生也说没想到记录工作要花这么多时间。

questions.question: What did May find that was particularly interesting?

analyses.content: Interestingly, there weren’t any bits of pottery there like you would expect to find, but I did get out some pieces of cloth and what looked like one or two silver beads. But our team leader said that they weren’t...
你可能听到 silver beads（银珠子）想选 C，但女生紧接着说领队指出那不是珠宝，而是用来织布的铅坠。
女生明确说虽然没发现陶器，但她确实挖出了一些“布料（pieces of cloth）”，这对应选项 A 的 fabric。

analyses.content: They seemed to have had a much better diet than I expected — fish and wheat, as well as oats, honey and fruit, lots of different things.
你可能听到 tall（高）想选 C，但录音说古人比现代人更高，而选项 C 说的是“不如现代人高”，意思反了。
男生说那些人吃的比预想的好，有鱼、小麦、燕麦、蜂蜜和水果，“很多不同的东西”，对应选项 A 的食物多样化。

questions.question: What do Tomas and May both say about the people they worked with?

analyses.content: It was tough for us all though, getting up at dawn every day and being out until late afternoon. Oh, that’s true enough. We were all exhausted...
不要选 A 或 C，因为只有男生的团队是“来自世界各地”且“年轻”的，女生的团队主要是英美人且年纪较大，这不是共同点。
两人都提到每天黎明起床一直干到下午晚些时候，大家都“筋疲力尽（exhausted）”，说明工作很辛苦。

analyses.content: 录音说确定挖掘地点后，去工地小屋拿任何你需要的“工具（tools）”，对应选项 H。
Now I think that when you’ve decided where to excavate, you go to the site hut and get whatever tools you need. Then clean the area, so you know exactly how big it’s going to be.
注意动词 get/take 的对象，录音先说拿 tools，然后再 clean the area，顺序不要搞反。
You then attach them to a record sheet which you get from the team leader, remembering to put in the site code, unit number and time.
不要听到 site code 或 unit number 就想选 F，这些是填在记录表里的内容，而不是你从领队那拿到的东西。
录音提到你要把照片附在一张从领队那里拿到的“记录表（record sheet）”上。
I think you then have to draw up a detailed plan of where you’re digging and then measure the limits.
Draw up a plan 是固定搭配，听到 draw 就要反应过来是画图/计划，不要去选 measuring 相关的干扰项。
录音说你必须画一个你正在挖掘的地方的“详细平面图（detailed plan）”，对应选项 I 的 comprehensive plan。
Now you can start with the trowel. But first you have to get soil samples and you keep them for further analysis.
你可能听到 analysis 就想选 G，但 analysis 是后期的目的，当前步骤的动作是 take samples。
录音强调在开始挖掘前，首先必须获取“土壤样本（soil samples）”并保存以供分析。
Yes. And if you make any finds, that is any object you retrieve, including animal bones, stone, as well as artefacts, they should all be registered and labelled.
题目空格是 "put ... on objects"，动词 label 变成名词 labels 填进去正好符合语境，不要直接选 C（objects）。
录音说任何发现的物品都应该被登记并且“贴标签（labelled）”，对应流程图里的 "Register and put labels on objects"。
